# QS-CFW-1159-60 - Quality specification - track link CFW-1159-60 (15B37)

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-1159-60

## Scope
This quality specification establishes acceptance criteria, inspection practices, and nonconformance handling for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) produced at Plant P3. It applies to all forged, heat treated, and machined track links delivered under part number CFW-1159-60 for customer orders and internal inventory. The document defines required measurements, allowable tolerances, inspection methods, documentation to be retained, and disposition instructions for nonconforming material.

Background and intent: track links are safety-critical wear components. The controls in this specification are intended to ensure dimensional accuracy, material condition, and hardness consistent with design requirements and downstream assembly fitment. Where measurement choices require judgment, the inspection method section provides examples and rationale to support consistent application by quality and production personnel.

## Requirements

| Item | Requirement | Acceptance |
|------|-------------|------------|
| Hardness | The hardness range for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is 36-40 HRC. | Must be within stated range across inspected locations. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is ±0.03 mm. | Measured bore diameter must be within nominal plus or minus stated tolerance. |
| Forging weight | The maximum forging weight for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is 80.0 kg. | Raw forging weight must not exceed stated maximum. |

Notes on table application: Acceptance applies to sampled or 100 percent inspected parts as specified in the production routing and as required by the purchase order. References to "nominal" in the bore entry refer to the drawing nominal diameter called out on the engineering drawing for CFW-1159-60.

## Inspection method

General approach: Inspection shall verify each requirement in the table using calibrated instruments and documented procedures. Inspectors shall be trained on the equipment and methods used and shall follow practices that minimize measurement variation.

Hardness measurement
- Hardness shall be verified using a Rockwell hardness tester calibrated to the HRC scale and operated per the instrument manufacturer's procedure. Impact of surface finish and case depth shall be considered; measures shall be taken to ensure a representative test surface (for example, removal of heavy scale, light surface grinding to reveal base material if required). When testing multiple locations, select points representative of typical load-bearing areas and areas away from heavy machining features. Record individual readings and calculate the observed range for the part lot. The acceptance criterion is the stated requirement in the requirements table.

Bore diameter measurement
- Bore diameter shall be measured using appropriately calibrated bore gauges, internal micrometers, or coordinate measuring machines capable of resolving the stated tolerance. When using manual plug gauges for quick checks, they are suitable only for go/no-go acceptance and must be supplemented by dimensional measurement during initial lot qualification or when process variation is suspected. For CMM measurement, use a probing strategy that avoids runout artifacts and records the measured nominal diameter for each bore. The stated tolerance is applied directly to the nominal drawing dimension.

Forging weight verification
- Forging weight shall be established at the forging operation by weighing the forged blank on calibrated scales. The maximum forging weight is the limit for feedstock and die charges. Record the weight for each heat or batch as part of the batch manufacturing record. If trimming operations remove material before subsequent operations, ensure the raw forging weight at release does not exceed the stated maximum.

Examples and rationale
- Example: A batch of track links with hardness readings of 37 HRC, 38 HRC, and 36 HRC is acceptable because all readings fall within the stated hardness range. An isolated reading below the stated range requires disposition per nonconformance handling.
- Example: A bore measured at nominal plus 0.02 mm is acceptable; a bore measured at nominal plus 0.04 mm is not acceptable against the stated tolerance.

Calibration and equipment
- All measuring equipment used to verify the requirements must be in calibration and traceable to internal calibration records. Calibration records and equipment identification must be retained in the quality record for the lot.

Records to keep
- Heat/batch manufacturing record including forging weight for each forged blank.
- Hardness test records showing individual readings, test locations, test instrument identification, and operator initials.
- Dimensional inspection report for bore diameters with instrument identification and measurement method.
- Calibration certificates for hardness tester, bore measurement devices, scales, and CMM probes used for the inspections.

## Nonconformance handling

Identification and segregation
- Any part or lot that fails to meet a requirement in the requirements table shall be clearly marked and physically segregated to prevent unintended use. Segregation shall be maintained until a disposition decision is recorded.

Disposition process
- The case shall be documented with the observed nonconformance, measured values, inspection evidence, and batch manufacturing records. The responsible quality engineer shall initiate a formal disposition. Possible dispositions include rework, repair, use-as-is with approval, or scrap. Rework or repair must be evaluated to ensure no compromise to material integrity or part function.

Required documentation
- Nonconformance reports shall include batch identity, forging weight record, hardness test records, dimensional inspection records, and photographs where applicable. The report shall describe containment actions and recommended disposition. The final disposition must be recorded and signed by the authorized quality representative.

Containment and corrective actions
- For process deviations that produce out-of-specification characteristics, containment measures shall include additional inspection of suspect lots and review of upstream process steps. Root-cause analysis and corrective actions shall be documented and retained with the nonconformance record.

Retention and audit
- All records described under Records to keep and nonconformance documentation shall be retained per the plant document control policy and made available for internal audit and customer review on request.

Revision control
- Changes to this specification shall be controlled through the plant document control process.
